title: Correlate operator config drift to upgrade failures and add live hotpatch fallback
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Several Private/VPC customers experienced failed operator/Helm-driven upgrades where the operator reconcile loop crashed or looped due to subtle config drift between tenant manifests and operator-managed defaults. This ticket tracks root-cause correlation work, a small hotpatch that enables safe in-place fallback, and a longer-term drift-detection instrumentation + automated recovery feature.

Background: We received 3 escalations in the last 48 hours (CUST-4381, CUST-4402, CUST-4410). Common symptoms: helm upgrade hangs at post-upgrade hook, operator controller restarts from OOM or panic, and subsequent Helm reconciles produce 409/412 errors. Initial triage shows tenant CRs containing deprecated/legacy fields or missing annotations that the new operator expects; however those fields were previously tolerated due to implicit defaults. The upgrade path removed a shim that compensated for missing keys, so the new operator hits an unhandled code path.

Goals:
1) Provide an immediate customer-safe hotpatch (0.1 release) that detects problematic CRs and routes tenants to a guaranteed fallback operator variant without requiring cluster rollback.
2) Implement correlation logic in operator telemetry to map specific config-drift signatures to upgrade failures so SRE/SE can preemptively quarantine at-risk tenants during future staged upgrades.
3) Deliver a permanent reconciler hardening and migration prune that either backfills tolerated defaults or rejects dangerous contract violations with clear remediation instructions.

What success looks like:
- Customers with the identified signatures can be repaired without cluster-wide rollbacks.
- Future upgrades surface a radar of at-risk tenants before traffic is cut over.
- Post-release, incident rate for onprem upgrades reduces by >= 85% for drift-related failures in the next three cycles.

Scope: Hotpatching operator image and Helm chart, small control-plane runtime checks, additional metrics + traces, documentation and runbook for SE/CS, and an automated preflight detection job for existing tenant manifests.

Non-goals: Full two-way schema migration CLI (would be tracked separately). Avoid touching tenant PVC/state; changes must be non-destructive.

Risk & rollback: Hotpatch is additive and will opt-in per-tenant (routing flag). If evidence of false positives appears, we will disable the routing flag and fallback to a conservative no-op path. Rollback plan includes immediate repinning to previous operator image and re-running Helm rollback if necessary (runbook link below).

incident_summary: Three onprem customer clusters failed operator upgrades due to config contract drift after removing a compatibility shim. Symptoms: Helm post-upgrade hooks hang, operator reconcile panics or loops; customers reported degraded API surface and inability to perform subsequent upgrades. No data loss observed. Escalation to engineering and SRE for hotpatch and runbook activation.
remediation_steps: Create and publish operator hotpatch image (operator:2026.03.1-hotpatch) with runtime guards for missing keys
Publish Helm chart override that injects per-tenant routing flag (redwood.com/upgrade-safety) and apply to affected tenants
Run automated preflight job to surface tenant CRs that match known drift signatures and notify CS/SE via PagerDuty and a dedicated Slack channel
Instrument operator telemetry to emit 'drift_signature' with hashed signature for clustering and postmortem
Add migration controller to backfill safe defaults for tolerated fields in a non-destructive, rate-limited job
Communicate to customers: mitigation steps, temporary routing, next steps, and timeline (SEs to own outbound comms)
